To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

directed information is not suitable for deterministic systems, that restricted directed information is a suitable remedy, and that it recovers the graph structure correctly when there is enough information.

(a) the directed information measure, in its original form, loses power in the deterministic limit; (b) the restricted directed information measure recovers the correct network structure even in the deterministic limit, if the graph is uniquely identifiable; (c) the restricted directed measure is a natural extension of the original directed information measure.
Directed information is not powerful enough to recover the causal structure when all the variables are deterministic.
